land.text: Bernicia 'stretching from the Forth to the Tees' (Bernicia page)

predecessors.note: Bernicia page: 'Aethelfrith united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604'. The Bernicia dossier carries 604-612; this dossier starts on Cliopatria's first Northumbria shape, 612.

land.text: Deira, between the Humber and the Tees, under Aethelfrith's crown from about 604

predecessors.note: The Northumbria infobox gives 'Union of the crowns of Bernicia and Deira: 654', a different union (Oswiu's, after the murder of Oswine in 651); the Bernicia and Aethelfrith pages give c. 604.

land.text: the lands of the ealdormen of Bamburgh, north of the Tees, Cliopatria's last Northumbria shape

successors.note: Northumbria page: 'Last Viking king expelled by King Eadred: 954'; Eadred 'appointed Oswulf earl of the whole of Northumbria'. The England dossier holds Bamburgh as a vassal from Eamont (12 July 927) and absorbs it in 954.
Deira left the kingdom in 867; the Danelaw dossier holds Yorkshire from 878.

capitals.name: Bamburgh
capitals.note: The Northumbria page lists no capital in its infobox and calls Bamburgh 'the royal city of Bamburgh' in a footnote; no opened page names York as the capital of the united kingdom (the Kingdom of York page, 867-954, is the Viking kingdom of Deira). After 867 Bamburgh is the seat of the northern rump.

rulers.name: Æthelfrith
rulers.note: Page: 593[?] to 616 (another table 593/604[?] to 616); the dossier starts at Cliopatria's 612. The strip follows the page's list of unified Northumbrian kings; sub-kings (Alchfrith, Ælfwine) are omitted.

rulers.name: Oswiu
rulers.note: Late 642 to 15 February 670 (a split table: Bernicia 642-644, Oswine in Deira 644-651, Œthelwald in Bernicia 651-654/5, Oswiu over both from 654; another table prints 15 August 670).

rulers.name: Ceolwulf
rulers.note: Second reign, 732 to 737/8 on the page.

rulers.name: Ælla
rulers.title: usurper
rulers.note: 862/3/7 to 21 March 867, killed by the Danes at York.

rulers.name: Osberht
rulers.note: Listed again for 867 to 21 March 867, when he was killed by the Danes.

rulers.name: Ecgberht I
rulers.title: client king north of the Tyne
rulers.note: Danish puppet, 867 to 872. From 872 the page's list splits into a York column (Ricsige, Halfdan, the Viking kings) and a Bamburgh column with gaps (877-895, 918-947); the strip stops at Ecgberht I.

keyframe_review.note: 23,570 km2: Bernicia 'from the Forth to the Tees' and Deira under one crown. The Northumbria infobox gives no area; Bernicia page: Aethelfrith 'united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604', so Cliopatria's 612 start is eight years after the page's union (the Bernicia dossier carries 604-611). Same-size shape to 625.

23,548 km2, the 612 shape unchanged. Edwin takes the throne after Aethelfrith's death at the River Idle (c. 616, Aethelfrith page); the Edwin page has him expel Ceretic from Elmet 'in either 616 or 626', and the shape does not grow until 626, so either Elmet was already inside it or the 626 alternative is the one Cliopatria draws.

30,842 km2: the shape adds Lindsey (exactly the Kingdom of Lindsey cells, 4.3 thousand km2), the Isle of Man and Anglesey (three cells), and a further ~11 cells (Dunoting and the north-west). Edwin page: 'From about 627 onwards, Edwin was the most powerful king among the Anglo-Saxons, ruling Bernicia, Deira and much of eastern Mercia', with the Isle of Man and Anglesey among his lands. The page does not name Lindsey; the one-year offset (626 shape, 'about 627' page) is within the precision of the era.

29,282 km2: the Man and Anglesey cells are gone. Edwin falls at Hatfield Chase (632 or 633) and 'Bernicia and Deira were again separated under two pagan kings' (year 633 has no Northumbria shape: Cliopatria draws Bernicia and Deira for that year); Oswald reunites the kingdom at Heavenfield in 634 (Bernicia page). Lindsey stays inside the shape through 681, although the Ecgfrith page has Ecgfrith 'seize' it only in 674: flagged in notes, not corrected, because no opened page says who held Lindsey 634-673.

35,714 km2: +6.8 thousand km2 between the Forth and the Tweed (27 cells, 3.7-1.5 W, 54.3-56.0 N). Gododdin page: 'In 638, Eidyn, modern Edinburgh, was under siege and fell to the Angles', and the Gododdin came under Bernician rule around then; the Gododdin lands are 'the Lothian and Borders regions of eastern Scotland'.

35,775 km2, unchanged. Oswiu page: Oswiu ruled Bernicia, 'from the River Tees to the Firth of Forth', while Deira was ruled by a separate king, Oswine, 'until about 651'. Cliopatria draws Deira inside the Northumbrian shape throughout; the Deira dossier ends in 634. Flagged in notes: a sub-kingdom, not a separate state on the map.

47,772 km2: +12.0 thousand km2 (44 cells, 3.4-2.2 W, 53.4-54.9 N), the size of Cliopatria's Rheged row (11,953 km2) which ends in 646. Rheged page: 'Rheged was taken over by Northumbria at some point before 730 AD'; Oswiu's marriage to Rhiainmellt 'probably in 638'. The year 647 is Cliopatria's, not the page's (confidence 1 in the ledger).

85,405 km2, the largest shape: the whole of Mercia as far south as 51.4 N is added. Oswiu page: after the Winwaed (655) 'Peada became king of southern Mercia, while Oswiu took the north'; Peada died 'probably at Easter 656' and Oswiu 'installed governors or subject kings in Mercia'; his 'total domination lasted only a short time, around three years'. The revolt that ended it is 'probably in late 659, but perhaps in 657', so the shape's end in 660 is the page's latest date.

47,772 km2, the 647 shape back. Mercia is lost (Oswiu page: Wulfhere 'installed as ruler of the Mercians'). The shape holds Lindsey (17 cells at 0.7 W-0.2 E, 53.0-53.65 N) to 681 and drops it only in the 682 shape; the Ecgfrith page has Ecgfrith 'seize the Kingdom of Lindsey' in 674 and Lindsey 'returned to the Mercians' after the Trent in 679, so the drop is three years late and the years 661-673 are doubtful. Not corrected: the pages opened say nothing on Lindsey for those years.

43,879 km2: Lindsey is gone (679 on the Ecgfrith page, three years before the shape). Ecgfrith dies at Dun Nechtain on 20 May 685; the page says Northumbria 'never regained the dominance of central Britain lost in 679; nor of northern Britain lost in 685', which fits a shape that never reached beyond the Forth even in 671-685 (Pictland was a tributary, see the ledger).

44,137 km2: +2 cells (506 km2, 2.9-1.9 W, 53.4-53.6 N), at the Mercian edge near the Peak. The Northumbria page names no territorial change at this date; recorded as a confidence-1 event. unverified: page budget.

43,718 km2 in shapes.csv plus Kyle (East Ayrshire, 7 cells, about 1,770 km2). Oengus I page: 'again in 750, when Kyle was taken from Alt Clut by Eadberht of Northumbria'; strathclyde /ledger/1 (confidence 3) is the loss and no Cliopatria Northumbria shape holds any East Ayrshire cell, so the gain is added here (ledger 750). No opened page says what became of Kyle later, so it stays in the shape to 866 and leaves with the 867 loss. Also: one cell (253 km2) at 54.99 N, 1.48 W (the Tyne at Newcastle) is dropped in the Cliopatria shape; the Northumbria page (reopened 2026-10-25) names no change at the Tyne, so raster noise is likely. unverified: page budget.

union.text: Kyle, central Ayrshire, taken from Alt Clut by Eadberht in 750

correction.text: the 750 shape plus Kyle ('Kyle was taken from Alt Clut by Eadberht of Northumbria', 750); Kyle is held until the Danes take York in 867 (ledger 867, confidence 1)
valid for 866 only: the whole kingdom, Bernicia and Deira, before the Danes take York, with Kyle (East Ayrshire)

keyframe_review.note: 41,835 km2: the whole kingdom, Deira included. Kingdom of York page: Ivar 'captured York in 866/ 867'; Ælla and Osberht killed in the battle of '21 March 867'; Northumbria page: 'Deira is conquered by Vikings: 867'. The shape holds for 866 only; from 867 the Deira cells (26 thousand km2, 103 cells) leave. Cliopatria removes them in 870, three years late (the Viking settlements row adds Yorkshire in 870). Kyle (East Ayrshire, taken from Alt Clut in 750) is added to the shape; it is dropped again by the 867 loss.

correction.text: Bernicia from the Tees to the Forth, the lands north of the Tyne and Tees left after the Danes took Deira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 867-869: the 870 shape (Bernicia only, 15,823 km2) from the year Deira is conquered. Northumbria page: 'Deira is conquered by Vikings: 867'; Ecgberht I ruled as a Norse client king from 867 to 872 in the north (Bernicia, north of the Tyne), Ricsige from 872, and in 874 Halfdan raided north of the Tyne and imposed rule on Bernicia. The rump keeps its shape and its name on the map; the client status is not drawn. Kyle (East Ayrshire) is not in this shape: see the 867 loss to nobody (confidence 1).

correction.text: the 870 shape unchanged, valid 870-899 only; about 900 the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle pass to Strathclyde (ledger 900) and the shape from 900 is keyframe kingdom-of-northumbria_900

keyframe_review.note: 15,823 km2: Bernicia from the Tees to the Forth (Northumberland, Durham, the Borders, Lothian, six cells of Cumbria near Carlisle). Valid 870-899. Rheged page: 'Around the year 900, after the power of Northumbria was destroyed by Viking incursions and settlement, large areas west of the Pennines fell without apparent warfare under the control of the Brittonic Kingdom of Strathclyde'; the six Cumbrian cells (1,517 km2) pass to Strathclyde about 900 (ledger loss), and the new keyframe 900-925 draws the shape without them. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 870..899 from this entry's own 'valid 870-899 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

minus.text: the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle that pass to Strathclyde about 900

correction.text: the 870 shape less the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle, 900-925: Bernicia from the Tees to the Forth, Cumbria left to Strathclyde

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 900-925, added after the review: Cliopatria keeps the six Cumbrian cells (1,517 km2, 61 cells remain) that the 900 loss gives to Strathclyde; the Rheged page has the western lands beyond the Pennines under Strathclyde 'around the year 900' without warfare. Strathclyde's dossier takes the same six cells together with the 20 cells Cliopatria draws in its Brythons row.

15,823 km2 in the Cliopatria shape (61 cells, about 15,400 km2, without Cumbria), unchanged to 935. Verdict changed from ok to adjust on review: the shape still holds the six Cumbrian cells that ledger 900 gives to Strathclyde. Æthelstan page (reopened 2026-10-25): on 12 July 927 Ealdred of Bamburgh accepted Æthelstan's overlordship at Eamont ('probably nominal', Ann Williams); the lands north of the Tees stayed outside the West Saxon shire system. The England dossier carries the vassal tint from 927 and this dossier now mirrors it (ledger 927).

minus.text: the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle that passed to Strathclyde about 900

correction.text: the 926 shape less the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle: the Bamburgh lands from the Tees to the Forth, an English vassal from the Eamont meeting of 12 July 927

minus.text: the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle that passed to Strathclyde about 900

correction.text: the lands of the ealdormen of Bamburgh (Cliopatria's last shape less the Cumbrian cells), kept until Eadred's 954 settlement

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 936-954: Cliopatria has no Northumbria after 935 and its Kingdom of England shape starts 936, but the Northumbria page has the Bamburgh lands outside the English kingdom until Eadred: 'Last Viking king expelled by King Eadred: 954' and 'Oswulf earl of the whole of Northumbria'. The England dossier (vassal_start 927, vassal_end 954) uses this same shape. Corrected on review: the six Cumbrian cells of Cliopatria's 935 shape are removed, as in keyframes 900-925 and 926-935.

region.text: Bernicia 'from the Forth to the Tees' together with Deira

ledger.note: 612: Bernicia and Deira are one kingdom, Northumbria, under Aethelfrith. 'Aethelfrith united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604' (Bernicia page); the Northumbria infobox gives the union of the crowns as 654, a second union under Oswiu. 612 is the first year of Cliopatria's Northumbria shape; the Bernicia dossier carries 604-612 (confidence 1 for the date).

region.text: Elmet, 'a Cumbric-speaking kingdom' in the West Riding of Yorkshire (Bernicia page); the pages name no boundary

ledger.note: 616: Edwin expels Ceretic from Elmet. 'Edwin expelled Ceretic from the minor British kingdom of Elmet in either 616 or 626' (Edwin page); the 626 alternative is the year Cliopatria's shape grows. The Elmet dossier dates the conquest 616 or 617 from its own page.

c. 616: Edwin of Deira becomes king after Aethelfrith falls at the River Idle; the Bernician house gives way to the Deiran line. 'Afterward, Edwin became king of Deira and Bernicia' (Aethelfrith page, c. 616; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle footnote dates the sons' exile to 617). Same state, same colour (rule 2); the Bernician line returns with Oswald in 634.

region.text: the Brittonic region of north-west England, Cliopatria's Dunoting

ledger.note: 626: Dunoting joins Northumbria on the map. Cliopatria's Dunoting row ends in 625 and the Northumbria shape grows in 626; the Northumbria page does not mention Dunoting (the Dunoting dossier cites the Hen Ogledd page: 'absorbed by Anglian Northumbria in the 7th century'). Page silent: confidence 1. Dunoding page reopened 2026-10-25: it describes the Welsh Dunoding (Eifionydd and Ardudwy, 'a subordinate realm within Gwynedd until the line of rulers descended from Dunod expired in c. 925') and does not mention Northumbria; Cliopatria's shape for this row lies in the Yorkshire Dales (about 2.39-1.89 W, 53.66-54.41 N), so the row's Wikipedia title does not fit its shape. Still confidence 1.

region.text: Lindsey, the former kingdom of Lindsey (northern Lincolnshire)

ledger.note: c. 627: Edwin rules 'much of eastern Mercia'. 'From about 627 onwards, Edwin was the most powerful king among the Anglo-Saxons, ruling Bernicia, Deira and much of eastern Mercia' (Edwin page). The page does not name Lindsey; Cliopatria's 626 shape adds exactly the Lindsey cells (northern Lincolnshire), and the Lindsey dossier ends in 625.

region.text: the Isle of Man, listed among the lands Edwin ruled from about 627

ledger.note: c. 627: Edwin holds the Isle of Man. The Edwin page lists the Isle of Man and Anglesey among the lands he ruled from about 627; no conquest date and no previous owner are given, so the counterpart is 'nobody'.

region.text: Anglesey, among the lands Edwin ruled from about 627

ledger.note: c. 627: Edwin holds Anglesey. The Edwin page lists the Isle of Man and Anglesey among his lands from about 627 (the Gwynedd dossier reads Bede on a different page and dates the taking of Anglesey 629).

region.text: Anglesey, held by Edwin from about 627

ledger.note: 12 October 633: Edwin falls at Hatfield Chase and Anglesey and the Isle of Man leave Northumbria. 'Edwin faced Penda and Cadwallon at the Battle of Hatfield Chase in 632 or 633', infobox 'death 12 October 632/633'. The page does not say what became of the two islands: Anglesey returns to Gwynedd in the Gwynedd dossier; Cliopatria's 634 shape drops both. Confidence 2: the loss is read from the shape.

region.text: the Isle of Man, Edwin's from about 627

ledger.note: 633: the Isle of Man leaves Northumbria with Edwin's fall. Page silent: the Edwin page does not mention the island after the list of Edwin's lands; Cliopatria's 634 shape drops its two cells.

region.text: Bernicia of 633 under Eanfrith

ledger.note: 633: Bernicia stands alone again. 'After his death, Bernicia and Deira were again separated under two pagan kings': Eanfrith ruled Bernicia and Osric Deira (Edwin page). Cliopatria draws no Northumbria shape for 633; its Bernicia and Deira rows hold the year.

region.text: Deira of 633 under Osric

ledger.note: 633: Deira stands alone again under Osric ('Osric ruled Deira ... Eanfrith ruled Bernicia', Edwin page).

region.text: Deira, reunited with Bernicia in 634

ledger.note: 634: Oswald wins Heavenfield and Bernicia is reunited with Deira. 'Oswald finally defeated Cadwallon at the Battle of Heavenfield in 634' and Bernicia 'was united with Deira to form Northumbria'. Eanfrith of Bernicia is dead (killed by Cadwallon); Oswald is the Bernician line restored.

region.text: Bernicia of 633, reunited in 634

ledger.note: 634: Bernicia rejoins the kingdom under Oswald, son of Aethelfrith (Bernicia page).

region.text: the Gododdin lands, the Lothian and Borders regions of eastern Scotland

ledger.note: 638: Edinburgh falls to the Angles. 'In 638, Eidyn, modern Edinburgh, was under siege and fell to the Angles, for the Gododdin seem to have come under the rule of Bernicia around this time.' Cliopatria's shape grows by 27 cells between the Forth and the Tweed in the same year.

region.text: Rheged, 'a large part of modern Cumbria' with parts of Dumfries and Galloway and possibly Lancashire

ledger.note: 647: Rheged is absorbed. The Rheged page says only that it 'was taken over by Northumbria at some point before 730 AD' and that Oswiu's marriage to Rhiainmellt was 'probably in 638', with a takeover that may have been peaceful. 647 is the first year of the Northumbria shape that contains Cliopatria's Rheged (its row ends 646); the year is Cliopatria's, not the page's. Rheged page reopened 2026-10-25: 'Rheged was annexed by Northumbria, some time before AD 730'; the Oswiu-Rieinmelth marriage was 'probably in 638, so it is possible that it was a peaceful takeover' with 'both kingdoms being inherited by the same man'. No year on the page for the annexation: confidence stays 1.

region.text: the whole of Mercia: the north taken by Oswiu, the south under Peada, then governors or subject kings

ledger.note: 655-656: Oswiu kills Penda at the Winwaed and takes Mercia. 'Oswiu took the north of the kingdom' and Peada became king of southern Mercia; Peada died 'probably at Easter 656' and Oswiu 'then installed governors or subject kings in Mercia'. The page gives 655 for the Winwaed (no month) and no boundary between Oswiu's north and Peada's south; Cliopatria draws all of Mercia from 656. The Mercia dossier has the same event at 656.

region.text: Mercia, lost to Wulfhere's revolt

ledger.note: c. 659: Mercia throws Oswiu off. 'Immin, Eata, and Eadberht led a revolt that installed Penda's son Wulfhere as ruler of the Mercians and drove out Oswiu's supporters', dated 'probably in late 659, but perhaps in 657'. Wulfhere 'apparently still recognised his primacy'. The Mercia dossier dates the revolt 658 from another page; Cliopatria keeps Mercia in the shape to 660.

region.text: Pictland, the land north of the Forth

ledger.note: 671: Ecgfrith defeats the Picts at the Battle of Two Rivers and the Northumbrians 'took control of Pictland for the next fourteen years' (Ecgfrith page). The page does not map Pictland; north of the Forth is the reading. A tributary Pictland, not Northumbrian territory in Cliopatria's shapes (none passes 56.0 N).

region.text: Lindsey, the former kingdom of Lindsey (northern Lincolnshire)

ledger.note: 674: Ecgfrith repels Wulfhere and takes Lindsey. 'Ecgfrith repelled the Mercian king Wulfhere, which let him seize the Kingdom of Lindsey' (Ecgfrith page). Cliopatria already has Lindsey inside the shape from 626; the Mercia dossier records the same year as contest_start.

region.text: Lindsey, the former kingdom of Lindsey (northern Lincolnshire)

ledger.note: 679: Lindsey is returned to Mercia. 'At the Battle of the Trent, fought against the Mercians under Æthelred, Ecgfrith's brother Ælfwine was killed. After Archbishop Theodore intervened, Lindsey was returned to the Mercians.' Northumbria 'never regained the dominance of central Britain lost in 679'. Cliopatria's shape drops Lindsey in 682.

region.text: Pictland, the land north of the Forth

ledger.note: 20 May 685: Ecgfrith is killed at Dun Nechtain and Pictland is lost. 'At the Battle of Dun Nechtain (Nechtansmere), Ecgfrith was killed and most of his army was lost'; Northumbria 'never regained ... northern Britain lost in 685'. The Northumbria page: the battle 'halted their expansion north and established a border' with the Picts.

region.text: two cells at the south-western edge, around Manchester and the Peak District

ledger.note: 705: Cliopatria's shape adds two cells (506 km2) at the Mercian edge around Manchester and the Peak, 2.9-1.9 W, 53.4-53.6 N. The Northumbria page records no change at this date: page silent. Counterpart named from the neighbour list (Mercia touches Northumbria 661-829). Mercia page reopened 2026-10-25: silent on any Mercian-Northumbrian border change around 700-710 (it says only that Manchester 'was the most northern extent of the kingdom, and at certain times was claimed by Northumbria and Danelaw', undated). Confidence stays 1.

region.text: Kyle, central Ayrshire

ledger.note: 750: Eadberht takes Kyle from the Britons of Alt Clut. 'again in 750, when Kyle was taken from Alt Clut by Eadberht of Northumbria' (Oengus I page), the year of the defeat at Mocetauc and six years before the joint attack of Oengus and Eadberht on Dumbarton (1 August 756). Mirrors strathclyde /ledger/1; Cliopatria draws East Ayrshire in Strathclyde's shapes and in no Northumbria shape.

region.text: one cell at the Tyne

ledger.note: 750: Cliopatria drops one cell (253 km2) on the Tyne at Newcastle, 54.99 N 1.48 W. The Northumbria page records no change: page silent, probably raster noise. Northumbria page reopened 2026-10-25: silent on the 8th-century borders and on the Tyne.

region.text: Northumbria, which 'acknowledged his overlordship' (Wessex dossier wording); the Northumbrian kingdom of 829 with Kyle

ledger.note: 829: the Northumbrians submit to Ecgberht of Wessex at Dore. 'Later in 829, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Ecgberht received the submission of the Northumbrians at Dore' (Egbert of Wessex page), the year he 'invaded Mercia and drove Wiglaf, the king of Mercia, into exile'. The Northumbria page is silent on Dore (checked). Mirrors kingdom-of-wessex /ledger/18.

region.text: Northumbria, the vassal of 829

ledger.note: 830: the overlordship lapses. The Egbert page gives no end to the tie: its only 830 entry is that 'Mercia regained its independence under Wiglaf' and it does not mention Northumbria in 830, so the end is bridged to the year Wessex's own dossier uses (kingdom-of-wessex /ledger/20). Page silent: confidence 1.

region.text: Kyle, central Ayrshire

ledger.note: 867: Kyle drops out of the drawn kingdom with the Danish conquest of Deira. No opened page says what became of Kyle after 750 (the Oengus I page ends its account of it at Eadberht's taking), the 867-869 rump is Cliopatria's Bernicia shape, which holds no East Ayrshire, and the holder is unknown, so the land goes to nobody. Page silent: confidence 1.

region.text: Deira, the land from the Humber to the Tees with York, and the Elmet and Lindsey cells of the 866 shape

ledger.note: 21 March 867: the Danes take York and Deira is lost. Kingdom of York page: Ivar 'captured York in 866/ 867' and the Anglo-Saxon leaders (Ælla and Osberht) were killed in 'the battle of 21 March 867'; Northumbria page: 'Deira is conquered by Vikings: 867'. Cliopatria removes Deira from the shape only in 870 and gives it to its Viking settlements row.

region.text: Cumbria beyond the Pennines: the six cells of the Northumbria shape inside Cumbria

ledger.note: c. 900: Strathclyde takes the land beyond the Pennines. Rheged page: 'around 900, after Viking attacks weakened Northumbria, western lands beyond the Pennines came under Strathclyde, apparently without warfare', Cumbria staying under Strathclyde until the early 11th century. Of Cliopatria's shape only six cells near Carlisle lie in Cumbria; the rest of Cumbria is drawn in its Brythons row. Strathclyde's /ledger/3 takes these six cells together with the 20 cells Cliopatria draws in its Brythons row (26 Cumbrian cells in all); keyframes 900-925, 926-935 and 936-954 here draw the shape without them.

minus.text: the Cumbrian cells already ceded to Strathclyde

region.text: Ealdred of Bamburgh's lands north of the Tees, the 926 shape less Cumbria

ledger.note: 12 July 927: Ealdred of Bamburgh accepts Æthelstan's overlordship at Eamont, near Penrith, along with Constantine II of Alba, Hywel Dda and Owain of Strathclyde (or Morgan ap Owain of Gwent). The submission 'was probably nominal' (Ann Williams, Æthelstan page). The Bernicia page: Ealdred 'accepted West Saxon overlordship'; the Northumbria infobox: 'Bernicia accepts the rule of King Æthelstan: 927'; the lands north of the Tees stayed outside the West Saxon shire system. Recoded on review from a rename to a vassal_start: it mirrors kingdom-of-england /ledger/2 (vassal_start 927, vassal_end 954); the state, its colour and its name stay.

minus.text: the Cumbrian cells ceded to Strathclyde

region.text: the Bamburgh lands north of the Tees, vassal of the English kings since 927

ledger.note: 954: the vassal earldom of Bamburgh becomes part of England's Northumbria. 'Last Viking king expelled by King Eadred: 954' and Eadred 'appointed Oswulf earl of the whole of Northumbria' (Northumbria page); the English side is kingdom-of-england /ledger/14 (vassal_end 954).

minus.text: the Cumbrian cells ceded to Strathclyde

region.text: the lands of the ealdormen of Bamburgh, north of the Tees, joined with York as the earldom of Northumbria (Cliopatria's last shape less Cumbria)

ledger.note: 954: Eadred ends Northumbria. 'Last Viking king expelled by King Eadred: 954'; Eric, murdered 'allegedly with the connivance of Oswulf' of Bamburgh, and Eadred then appointed Oswulf 'earl of the whole of Northumbria'. The Bamburgh lands become the English earldom; the Kingdom of York page: Stainmore ended Scandinavian rule and the earls who followed were appointed by the kings of England.

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Northumbrian victory: Aethelfrith 'defeated the Powysian army at Chester, killing King Selyf Sarffgadau'. The page names no territory gained and no frontier; some have seen it as splitting the Welsh Britons from the northern ones, but Koch calls that view outdated.

wars.name: Hatfield Chase and Cadwallon's invasion
wars.outcome: Edwin defeated and killed at Hatfield Chase (12 October 632/633) by Penda and Cadwallon; Bernicia and Deira separate under Eanfrith and Osric, both killed by Cadwallon; Oswald defeats Cadwallon at Heavenfield in 634 and reunites Northumbria.
wars.note: The Edwin page gives 632 or 633 for the battle; the Bernicia page gives 634 for Heavenfield.

wars.name: Winwaed campaign

zones.text: Mercia: Oswiu took the north, Peada the south

wars.outcome: Oswiu kills Penda at the Winwaed (655, near Loidis) and holds Mercia until the revolt of 'probably late 659, but perhaps 657' installed Wulfhere.
wars.note: Penda's forces had reached the gates of Bamburgh before 651.

wars.name: Northumbrian-Pictish war
wars.outcome: Ecgfrith's victory at the Battle of Two Rivers (671) puts Pictland under Northumbrian control for fourteen years; Ecgfrith is killed at Dun Nechtain on 20 May 685 and the Picts regain their independence.

wars.name: Northumbrian-Mercian war over Lindsey

zones.text: Lindsey, the former kingdom of Lindsey (northern Lincolnshire)

wars.outcome: Ecgfrith repels Wulfhere and seizes Lindsey (674); Ælfwine is killed at the Trent (679) and Lindsey is returned to Mercia after Archbishop Theodore's intervention.

wars.name: Viking conquest of Northumbria
wars.outcome: The Great Heathen Army lands in East Anglia (865); Ivar takes York (866/867); Ælla and Osberht die on 21 March 867 and Deira is conquered; the north is left as a Norse client kingdom under Ecgberht I (867-872).
wars.note: Northumbria page: 'The Vikings strike York twice' in 866-867.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives for the whole life. The only dated frontier on the pages is the border with the Picts 'established' by Dun Nechtain (685), which the shapes do not draw; the Tweed boundary of the earldom is undated on the Northumbria page.

notes: Nine pages were budgeted; ten were opened because the 638 shape step (Edinburgh) needed the Gododdin page. Cliopatria's start 612 is the first Northumbria shape; the pages put the union of Bernicia and Deira at c. 604 (Bernicia, Aethelfrith) or 654 (Northumbria infobox), and the sibling Bernicia/Deira dossiers carry 604-612, so this dossier starts at 612. The year 633 has no Northumbria shape: Cliopatria draws Bernicia and Deira for it; the ledger records loss/gain with those two dossiers (633/634). Lindsey sits inside every shape from 626 to 681 though the pages opened give only 627-633 (Edwin, 'much of eastern Mercia'), 655-659 (inside Oswiu's Mercia) and 674-679 (Ecgfrith); 634-673 is doubtful and was not corrected because no page says who held Lindsey then; the Mercia dossier cites a Mercian Supremacy page that dates a Mercian loss of Lindsey to 661. Oswine's separate Deira (to about 651) and the Norse client kings of Bernicia (Ecgberht I 867-872, Ricsige 872) are sub-kingships inside one drawn kingdom. The state continues to 954 (not Cliopatria's 935) because the England dossier carries Bamburgh as a vassal 927-954; a new keyframe 936-954 reuses Cliopatria's last shape. Dissent between pages: Northumbria infobox 654 vs Bernicia/Aethelfrith c. 604 for the union; Edwin page Elmet 616 or 626 vs the Elmet dossier's 616 or 617; Oswiu page revolt 657 or late 659 vs the Mercia dossier's 658. Counterparts needing a dossier: kingdom-of-elmet, picts and gododdin exist as siblings' dossiers; no Northumbrian-rump 'Bamburgh' dossier exists (the Northumbria dossier carries it). Ruler strip omitted: no list page was opened. Quotation marks enclose strings the page-fetch tool returned as quotations; other wording paraphrases its summary of the page, which was read by WebFetch only (no raw page text). REPAIR 2026-10-25 (review eu-11-g): (1) keyframes 926 and 936-954 are now adjust, with the six Cumbrian cells near Carlisle removed (Rheged page: Strathclyde took the lands beyond the Pennines about 900); the 870 keyframe is valid 870-899 and a new keyframe 900-925 carries the shape without them. (2) The Eamont meeting of 12 July 927 is now a vassal_start with kingdom-of-england, ended by a vassal_end in 954, mirroring England's ledger (the Æthelstan page was reopened). (3) Kyle: Strathclyde's 750 loss now has its gain here (Oengus I page, reopened), keyframes 750 and 866 hold East Ayrshire, and a confidence-1 loss to nobody in 867 closes it because no opened page says what became of Kyle later. (4) Dore: vassal_start 829 and vassal_end 830 with kingdom-of-wessex from the Egbert of Wessex page; the Northumbria page does not mention Dore; the end year is Wessex's own bridge (confidence 1). (5) Thin items: Dunoting 626 stays confidence 1 because the Dunoding page is about the Welsh Dunoding and does not mention Northumbria (Cliopatria's row, in the Yorkshire Dales, carries a Wikipedia title that does not fit it); Rheged 647 stays at 1 ('some time before AD 730'); the 705 and 750 cell moves stay at 1 (Mercia and Northumbria pages silent). (6) Rulers added for 612-872 from the List of monarchs of Northumbria; the page's later Viking-era entries are split between York and Bamburgh with gaps and are not carried. I do not disagree with any finding; the Wessex 829 tie is mirrored at the Wessex dossier's own confidence.
